# A predeclared PluralKey constant is recognized by the select's type, not by
# the operand's spelling. Keying off the name "i18n" read the constant only
# when the import was unaliased; under `import t "sngl:i18n"` the JS backend
# emitted the alias as a bare identifier, `{ [t.one]: ... }`, which is a
# ReferenceError at runtime.

sngl generate --platform html --lang none -o outalias alias.sngl
grep '\["one"\]: "one item"' outalias/index.html
grep '\["other"\]: "many items"' outalias/index.html
! grep 't\.one' outalias/index.html

# The unaliased spelling emits the same thing.
sngl generate --platform html --lang none -o outplain plain.sngl
grep '\["one"\]: "one item"' outplain/index.html

-- alias.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import t "sngl:i18n"

component main {
    var n int = 2
    text(value=t.plural(n, {t.one = "one item", t.other = "many items"}))
}
-- plain.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import "sngl:i18n"

component main {
    var n int = 2
    text(value=i18n.plural(n, {i18n.one = "one item", i18n.other = "many items"}))
}
